text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
West Australian dietary reformer MARY FARRELLY, who wrote a booklet called "How to cook wheat" and constantly snacked on puffed wheat while lecturing women in rural areas, was born in 1866.
Australian bookmaker DANIEL GREEN was born in 1869.

Heroic Australian soldier THOMAS AXTON, who was awarded the Victoria Cross, was born in 1894. He attacked a German machine gun bunker during World War One and took six prisoners of war, single handedly.
American actress JEANETTE MCDONALD was born in 1901.
Northern Territory politician HAROLD BRENNAN was born in 1905.
Australian writer ROSEMARY DOBSON was born in 1920.
British actor IAN CARMICHAEL, who appeared in many light comedy roles, was born in 1920.
Australian actor NICK TATE was born in 1942.

Ex Beatle Sir (JAMES) PAUL MCCARTNEY was born in 1942. On the 11th of April, 1970, MCCARTNEY announced that he would never again record with JOHN LENNON, and six days later his first solo record appeared (which he had recorded at home). He formed the

band 'Wings' in 1971. His best known composition is probably "Yesterday", which is one of the most often-recorded songs. Until 1991, "Mull Of Kintyre" was the biggest selling single in the United Kingdom. It sold 2.5 million copies. PAUL was awarded a knighthood and a Grammy for his life's work.
British singer ALISON MOYET (GENEVIEVE ALISON-JANE MOYET), who was nicknamed "Alf" by her French father, was born in 1961.
** EVENTS **
1429 : The English, retreating after the siege of
Orleans, were attacked and defeated by French forces under JOAN of Arc and Duc D'ALENCON at the battle of Patay.
1583 : The first life insurance policy was issued in
London.
1815 : British and Prussian forces, under the command of
the DUKE OF WELLINGTON and Field Marshall GERHARD VON BLUCHER, finally defeated NAPOLEON BONAPARTE in the bloody Battle of Waterloo in Belgium.
1902 : British novelist SAMUEL BUTLER died.
1928 : Norwegian explorer ROALD AMUNDSEN, who reached the
South Pole ahead of Captain ROBERT SCOTT, died in a plane crash while attempting to rescue another explorer.
1928 : AMELIA EARHART became the first woman passenger to
fly the Atlantic Ocean, when the seaplane "Friendship" touched down at Burny Port in south Wales following a flight from Newfoundland.
1936 : Russian novelist MAXIM GORKI, who became the first
President of the Soviet Writers' Union, died.
1953 : Egypt was proclaimed a Republic with General
NEGUIB as its first President.
1959 : Academy award winning American stage and screen
actress ETHEL BARRYMORE died.
1975 : Prince FEISAL MUSAID was publicly beheaded in
Riyadh for the assassination of Saudi King FEISAL on March 25.
1975 : The first North Sea oil was pumped ashore in
Britain.
1977 : "Sex Pistol" singer JOHNNY ROTTEN was attacked by
thugs armed with razors in a North London pub.
1979 : American President JIMMY CARTER and Soviet leader

LEONID ILYICH BREZHNEV signed the historic 'Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty' in Vienna. CARTER surprised his Russian counterpart by hugging and kissing him on both cheeks following the signing of the documents.
1982 : The South Australian Government approved
legislation for the development of the controversial Roxby Downs project.
1984 : Australia's GREG NORMAN was beaten in a play-off
by American FUZZY ZOELLER, for the United States Golf Open title.
1994 : Former N.F.L. great O.J. SIMPSON was charged with

two counts of murder, over the deaths of his ex-wife and her male friend. Police arrested SIMPSON after chasing him through the streets of Los Angeles. The chase was televised around the world, as SIMPSON reportedly threatened to take his own life.
1996 : The U.S. Senate's Whitewater Committee issued a
scathing final report accusing President and Mrs CLINTON of a wide range of questionable conduct.
